description: Reference library for DJ-gent. Personas, Camelot wheel, slot templates, transition presets and crowd-reading heuristics. Edit freely — read at startup.

personas.name: Warehouse Techno
personas.bio: Long-form melodic and driving techno. Hypnotic, machine-led, builds slowly and rewards patience. Camelot 7A-11A territory, mostly minor.

set_style.energy_arc: Slow ramp from 4/10 to 9/10 over 90 minutes. No sub-7 dips after the first hour.
set_style.vocals: sparse — granular textures and one-shots only
do: honor the first drop of the incoming track — never cut over it
blend for at least 32 bars when keys are compatible
use the breakdown of the outgoing track as the runway
dont: double-drop unless both tracks are <128 bpm and harmonically related
stack two melodic leads — kill one with EQ before the swap
tease a vocal hook you don't deliver inside 16 bars

personas.name: Peak Tech-House
personas.bio: Peak-time tech and tribal house. Drum-forward, vocal hooks, festival energy. Camelot is flexible — groove > harmony in this lane.

set_style.energy_arc: Open at 7/10, hold 8-9/10 across the slot, one breath at the 60% mark.
set_style.vocals: expected — hooks, stabs, a cappellas overlaid on grooves
do: ride the percussion bus — let the bongos overlap for 8 bars before the swap
use a vocal hook from track B as the announcement on track A's outro
drop short loops on the kick to extend tension before a slam
dont: let the energy dip below 7/10 for more than 16 bars
blend two basslines for more than 4 bars
play the same vocal a cappella twice in one set

personas.name: Sunrise / Closing
personas.bio: Closing slot, 5-7am. Emotional, slower, melodic. The crowd is tired but locked in — reward them with payoff, not novelty.

set_style.energy_arc: 8/10 at the open (still peak), wind down to 5/10 by the close. No spikes.
set_style.vocals: yearning, lyrical — full vocal cuts encouraged
do: blend long. 64 bars is normal, 96 isn't unusual
drop a known emotional anchor track in the last 30 minutes
raise the key one Camelot tick every 3-4 tracks for lift
dont: hard-cut — the transition itself is part of the comedown
pull the bass on the last track until the lights are coming up

personas.name: Warm-up
personas.bio: First two hours of a 6-hour night. Dance-floor architect. Your job is to set the room up for the headliner, not steal the spotlight.

set_style.energy_arc: Open at 3/10, end at 6/10. Never cross 7.
set_style.vocals: spoken word, dub vocals, dub-style delays only
do: leave headroom — the headliner needs somewhere to take it
start below 120 bpm and creep up 1 bpm every 20 minutes
use rare and deep cuts the crowd won't recognise
dont: drop a peak-time anthem in the warmup
exceed 124 bpm before the headliner is on
fill the dance floor in the first 20 minutes — let it breathe

camelot_wheel.description: Camelot notation. Number = position on the wheel (1-12). Letter A = minor, B = major. Compatible mixes: same number, +/- 1 number same letter, or same number flip letter (energy boost).

phases.name: Settle
phases.notes: establish the room, don't fill the floor

phases.name: Open
phases.notes: first heads on the floor, deep grooves

phases.name: Hand-off
phases.notes: set up the headliner — leave the room hungry

phases.name: Open
phases.notes: land hard but leave room to climb

phases.name: Breath
phases.notes: one melodic / vocal track to reset attention

phases.name: Send-off
phases.notes: biggest record last 20 min, end on a banger

phases.name: Continue
phases.notes: carry the previous DJ's energy, don't reset

phases.name: Anchor
phases.notes: drop the emotional anchor track somewhere here

phases.name: Lift-up
phases.notes: key-shift +1 every other track, vocals welcome

phases.name: Last record
phases.notes: the goodbye record — they'll talk about this for years if you nail it

transition_presets.name: Long blend
moves: drop track B at bar 33 of track A's outro
swap basslines on the next 16-bar boundary using EQ low cut on A
swap leads at the 32-bar mark using EQ mid cut on A
filter A out over the final 8 bars while B's drop arrives
kill A's channel only after B's first downbeat

transition_presets.name: EQ swap
moves: align downbeats at the 16-bar boundary
kill A's lows, bring B's lows in, on the same beat
swap mids 8 bars later
use the percussion of both tracks to glue — don't EQ-cut highs
pull A's channel on the next 16-bar boundary

transition_presets.name: Loop tease + slam
transition_presets.best_for: peak-time hand-offs, when track A has a strong loopable bar
moves: find a 2-bar loop in A's drop section
loop it for 4-8 bars, raising filter cutoff each repeat
cue B at the next downbeat
kill A's loop entirely as B drops — no overlap
leave B clean for at least 16 bars before the next move

transition_presets.name: Double drop
transition_presets.key_rule: same Camelot number — anything else risks a clash
moves: phase-align both tracks at the bar before the drop
ride both faders up — the kicks must hit on the same downbeat
kill A's bassline immediately on the drop
B carries the drop, A's lead continues for 8 bars then EQ-out
do not attempt above 130 bpm without rehearsal

transition_presets.name: Filter sweep cross-fade
moves: high-pass A from full to 1 kHz over 8 bars
drop B on the next downbeat
high-pass B from 1 kHz back to full over 8 bars
let A ride underneath one bar past B's drop, then pull

cue_point_template.description: Default hot cue layout for a 4/4 dance track at typical structure. Adjust to track length and arrangement.

cues.label: A — Intro start
cues.purpose: phrase-aligned start, drop track in here

cues.label: B — First drop
cues.purpose: skip the intro on impatient nights

cues.label: C — Breakdown
cues.purpose: cue point for emotional reset or to ride a riser

cues.label: E — Final 16
cues.purpose: outro start — your runway for the next mix

cues.label: F — Acapella section
cues.purpose: if the track has a vocal-only bar, mark it for overlay use

cues.label: G — Loop point
cues.purpose: a clean 2 or 4-bar loop for tease-slam transitions

crowd_signals.diagnosis: energy too high too soon, or track is too dark
crowd_signals.pivot: drop one BPM, drop a familiar vocal hook on the next track
extend the current track, loop the breakdown, delay the next mix by 16 bars

crowd_signals.diagnosis: you've lost them — usually a long blend that doesn't pay off
crowd_signals.pivot: EQ-swap into a groove track at +2 energy, no melody

crowd_signals.diagnosis: drop landed wrong — bass mix or track choice
crowd_signals.pivot: next track must be a known anchor — no risks

crowd_signals.diagnosis: they're with you — don't show off
crowd_signals.pivot: stay the course, blend long, no genre swerves
next 30 minutes is your peak window, line up the heat
